Connor / team —

Attached is the rollout playbook (summary below) and I've also added a detailed canary-metrics.md to the shared drive. High-level plan:

1) Provisioning (T-7 days)
- Allocate new 8x A100 reserved pool in us-west-2 under CliApps tenancy. Pre-provision infra and AMIs.
- Smoke tests for model artifacts, quantization profile validation.

2) Dry run (T-3 days)
- Internal dry run with synthetic traffic to validate batching, KV hits, and prefix cache behavior.
- Validate rollback path: de-register new pool from routing and re-route back to legacy pool in <20 minutes.

3) Canary (Cutover day, hour 0)
- Start with 5% traffic to new pool for 2 hours. Monitor: 99th pct latency, 95th pct latency, error rate, GPU OOMs, token throughput.
- If stable, increase to 25% for next 2 hours. If metrics are within thresholds, proceed to 50% for 1 hour, then 100% steady shift over 4 hours.
- Canary abort thresholds: error rate >0.5% sustained over 5 minutes OR 99th pct latency > 2x baseline OR any OOMs. Abort triggers immediate rollback.

4) Gradual ramp / full shift (hours 6–10)
- Incremental shift steps with 30–60 minute observation windows.
- Final validation: end-to-end integration tests and customer smoke test.

5) Post-cutover (T+1 day)
- 24–72 hour heightened monitoring and weekly throughput reporting for first month.

Owners and contacts:
- SRE lead (on-call): Vivek Kulkarni (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai)
- Account lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai)
- Customer ops contact: Alyssa Park (alyssa.park@cliapps.com)

Runbooks and artifacts attached: cutover-checklist.xlsx, canary-metrics.md. I'll prepare dashboards for the specific canary widgets and share links.

Note on SLAs: To meet the throughput guarantee we'll enable autoscale headroom of 10% during the first 30 days. If production behavior deviates from our forecast we'll propose a capacity adjustment or temporary burst credits.

-Vivek
